facts.text: RAND Corporation is an independent American research institute, and the Government Accountability Office (GAO) is the audit arm of the United States Congress whose guides and program reviews address credible cost and schedule estimates.
facts.quote: RAND is an independent American research institute whose 2016 report showed that road miles alone cannot prove a self-driving car is safe, and GAO is the audit arm of the United States Congress

facts.text: RAND's Driving to Safety report by Kalra and Paddock, published in April 2016, calculated that autonomous vehicles would require hundreds of millions and sometimes hundreds of billions of road miles to demonstrate reliability.
facts.quote: RAND's report "Driving to Safety" (Kalra and Paddock, April 2016) calculated that autonomous vehicles "would have to be driven hundreds of millions of miles and sometimes hundreds of billions of miles"

facts.text: RAND's Driving to Safety calculated that 275 million failure-free miles would be needed to show, with 95 percent confidence, an autonomous-vehicle fatality rate no worse than the human rate of 1.09 per 100 million miles.
facts.quote: 275 million failure-free miles to show, with 95 percent confidence, a fatality rate no worse than the human rate of 1.09 per 100 million miles

facts.text: RAND's Driving to Safety calculated that about 11 billion miles would be needed to demonstrate a 20 percent improvement in autonomous-vehicle fatality rate over the human rate.
facts.quote: and about 11 billion miles to show a 20 percent improvement [Chapter 9]

facts.text: The booklet concludes that RAND's statistical logic transfers to off-road machines, but RAND's numerical road-mile estimates do not.
facts.quote: The booklet states that the logic transfers to off-road machines and the numbers do not

facts.text: Off-road machines accumulate far less exposure per unit than cars, making the exposure gap for demonstrating safety worse on a job site rather than better.
facts.quote: off-road machines accumulate far less exposure per unit than cars, "so the gap is worse on a job site, not better"

facts.text: The booklet identifies RAND's Driving to Safety report as the statistical reason virtual testing is pursued.

facts.text: RAND developed assumption-based planning in the 1990s, and the booklet adopts that method to track load-bearing assumptions.
facts.quote: RAND also developed assumption-based planning in the 1990s, which the booklet adopts for tracking load-bearing assumptions [Chapter 12].

facts.text: GAO audits federal programs, and its acquisition reviews link immature technology at the point of commitment to cost growth and delay.
facts.quote: The Government Accountability Office (GAO) audits federal programs. Its long series of acquisition reviews links immature technology at the point of commitment to cost growth and delay

facts.text: In GAO's 2006 acquisition evidence, most of 23 major defense programs began development with immature technologies, and 10 already expected more than 30 percent cost growth or a year's delay.
facts.quote: in 2006 most of 23 major defense programs began development with immature technologies and 10 already expected more than 30 percent cost growth or a year's delay

facts.text: A July 2026 GAO report covering 104 programs found that almost half entered with immature technologies and that average delivery time exceeded 12 years.
facts.quote: a July 2026 report on 104 programs found "almost half" entered with immature technologies and average delivery time above 12 years [Chapter 12].

facts.text: GAO's Schedule Assessment Guide (2015) provides ten best-practice areas and schedule-risk analysis.

facts.text: GAO's practical guidance includes the Cost Estimating and Assessment Guide (2020) and the Technology Readiness Assessment Guide (2020).

facts.text: GAO recommended iterative minimum viable products in 2025.

facts.text: GAO's principle of knowledge before commitment underlies the booklet's gate-based plan and its use of ranges instead of dates.
